claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me first check the official guidance to ensure I can provide you with accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for reaching out. To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 16, their eligibility depends on whether they're continuing in education or training.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an apprenticeship)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in school or college anymore, but they have started an apprenticeship recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one important detail about the apprenticeship.

Is Alex's apprenticeship in England specifically?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, actually it's not in England. Alex is doing their apprenticeship in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

Do you live with Alex in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester together. Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question to help determine your eligibility.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Since Alex is 16 and doing an apprenticeship, Child Benefit can normally continue until they're 20 if they're in approved education or training. The rules specifically state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child "starts an apprenticeship **in England**."

Because Alex's apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland (Belfast), not England, this exclusion doesn't apply to your situation. Since you:
- Live with Alex in the UK (Manchester)
- Are responsible for Alex who is under 20
- Alex is in approved training (an apprenticeship)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the government website or by contacting HMRC. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.
